subject: Post-call: DevKit & integration next steps (auth, routing, samples)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@lumina.ai>, Samira Patel <samira@lumina.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: DevKit & integration next steps (auth, routing, samples)

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track actions related to SDK setup, auth, routing, and sample apps for local testing.

Call summary (high level)
- Goal: Replace existing heuristic reranker with Redwood embeddings + reranker pipeline and adopt our TypeScript/ Python SDKs for inference calls.
- Constraints: Need private-network-friendly auth (service-account / mTLS), ability to route requests to dedicated capacity in us-west, and structured output/tool-calling for our extraction tasks.

Action items (suggested owner / timeline)
1) SDK quickstart + local sample apps (Python + TS) — Redwood to provide minimal repo and run instructions (target: devs can run end-to-end locally with a proxy token). Owner: Rafael. ETA: 3 working days.
2) Auth options doc — outline API key / service account / OAuth flows and recommended for private deployment. Owner: Redwood (Ben). ETA: 2 business days.
3) Routing / model variants — confirm model variants and routing policy for latency-sensitive endpoints (embed vs gen). Owner: Rafael + Marissa. ETA: 4 business days.
4) Embeddings + reranker wiring — provide sample pipeline (embedding -> kNN -> rerank). Include evaluation hooks. Owner: Lumina / Redwood collaborative. ETA: initial sample in 1 week.

Attachments: redwood-devkit-v1.zip (sample apps + README), integration-checklist.xlsx (action tracker). I attached the devkit bundle; it includes a small Python Flask proxy and a TS node sample that uses the SDK.

Questions for you (to confirm):
- Which internal CI environment should we target for the initial tests (GitHub Actions runner image, or an internal macOS/Linux runner)?
- Do you have a preference for service account + KMS or mTLS for private deployments?

Next suggested step: 60m technical deep dive with your infra + security (to validate auth & networking). We can run through the sample apps, env variables, and a short demo of prefix caching behavior. I’ll follow up with calendar options.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Alex Huang <alex.huang@lumina.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Samira Patel <samira@lumina.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: DevKit & integration next steps (auth, routing, samples)

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- CI target: We’ll start on GitHub Actions using an ubuntu-latest runner (we can mirror to internal runners later).
- Auth preference: Security leans toward service accounts backed by our KMS for key rotation. mTLS might be doable for on-prem but adds complexity initially.
- For routing, our SLA needs low single-digit 100ms p95 for short-generation endpoints; embeddings can be batched.

Requests from Lumina: 
1) Can you include a TypeScript sample that demonstrates: structured output -> tool-calling pattern (i.e., model returns a JSON payload with a tool call to a search/kb service) and a fallback path when the tool fails?
2) A Python notebook showing embedding generation and a simple kNN retrieval, with a script that runs a reranker (call to Redwood rerank endpoint) against the top 20 candidates.
3) Minimal instructions to run everything locally behind a proxy token (so we don’t have to open our network).

I took a look at the attached devkit — nice start. The infra diagram I mentioned is attached to this reply (lumina-infra-diagram.pdf). I’ll also pull Samira into the deep-dive scheduling.

— Alex
Alex Huang | Head of Integrations, Lumina AI
alex.huang@lumina.ai
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@lumina.ai>, Samira Patel <samira@lumina.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: DevKit & integration next steps (auth, routing, samples)

Alex / Samira — thanks, and great notes. Quick responses inline and a concrete quickstart below.

Auth: we will produce a short doc recommending service-account + KMS as the primary path for Private; we’ll include an mTLS appendix for on-prem customers. Ben will own the write-up and examples for getting service accounts + KMS rotation working with our SDK.

Routing: we’ll provide a routing policy example (yaml) to send low-latency endpoints to Dedicated us-west pools and batch-able workloads (embeddings) to general capacity. That will include a fallback policy to a cheaper variant when capacity is constrained.

Samples we’ll deliver (attached/devkit):
- ts-samples/tool-calling.ts — demonstrates structured JSON output and a simulated tool call to a local KB endpoint; includes a fallback logic path.
- python/samples/embeddings_rerank.ipynb — notebook that generates embeddings, builds a simple FAISS index (local), and calls Redwood rerank endpoint for final ordering.
- local-proxy/README.md — how to start a small local proxy that issues one-time dev tokens (no inbound ports required on your side).

Quickstart (minimal, run locally)
1) Unzip redwood-devkit-v1.zip
2) Set env vars: REDWOOD_API_HOST (use local proxy host), REDWOOD_AUTH_TOKEN (proxy token), NODE_ENV=development or PYTHON_ENV=development
3) For TS sample: cd ts-samples && npm ci && npm run demo (this runs a local KB stub and runs the tool-calling flow against the proxy)
4) For Python: cd python/samples && pip install -r requirements.txt && jupyter nbconvert --execute embeddings_rerank.ipynb --to notebook --output output.ipynb

I’ll upload a cleaned devkit and a link to a lightweight readme in Drive. HubSpot deal updated (LUM-2027-0421) with the action items.

Proposing deep-dive times (all PDT): Tue 2027-06-22 10:00, Tue 2027-06-22 15:00, Wed 2027-06-23 09:00. Alex/Samira — which works? I’ll send a calendar invite and add an infra call agenda (auth flows, demo, routing policy).

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
